steps.title: I2C LCD

quickCheck.question: Which standard library header file must be included in your Arduino sketch to provide I2C communication functions?
quickCheck.explanation: <Wire.h> is the built-in Arduino library that manages the ATmega328P Two-Wire Interface (I2C) hardware.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Recall Lesson 3: libraries provide pre-written driver code, and <Wire.h> is the universal Arduino library for I2C.

quickCheck.question: In the declaration LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27, 16, 2);, what information does the first argument 0x27 provide?
options: The 7-bit I2C bus hardware address of the display backpack.
The refresh rate of the LCD in frames per second.
The pin number where the contrast knob is connected.
quickCheck.explanation: The first parameter defines the I2C hardware address (0x27) so the library communicates with the correct physical backpack on the bus.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: In Step 4, we saw that every I2C device requires its specific 7-bit address to respond to incoming bus packets.

steps.title: Software Drivers: Wire.h and LiquidCrystal_I2C
steps.markdownContent:
### Software Driver Architecture

To control the LCD from C++, two libraries collaborate:

```
[ Your Monster Sketch: lcd.print("ROBOT ACTIVE!"); ]
                         │
                         ▼
[ LiquidCrystal_I2C Library: Translates text into character codes ]
                         │
                         ▼
[ Wire.h Library: Manages hardware TWI clock & byte packets ]
                         │
                         ▼ (SDA & SCL Pulses over A4 & A5)
[ PCF8574 Hardware Backpack ] ──► [ 16x2 LCD Glass Screen ]
```

### Essential Driver Methods:
- `LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27, 16, 2);`: Constructor setting address (0x27), columns (16), and rows (2).
- `lcd.init();`: Initializes the PCF8574 and LCD controller chip.
- `lcd.backlight();`: Powers the LED backlight on.
- `lcd.setCursor(col, row);`: Positions the text cursor (0-indexed: col 0–15, row 0–1).
- `lcd.print("Text");`: Renders characters on screen.

interactiveConfig.question: What do the coordinate arguments (0, 1) specify in lcd.setCursor(0, 1);?
options: Column 0 (far left) on Row 1 (the bottom line), because coordinates are zero-indexed
The number 01 is printed onto the screen
interactiveConfig.explanation: LCD coordinates are zero-indexed: columns run 0 to 15, and rows run 0 (top line) and 1 (bottom line).
